item.title: Tai Po blaze: NGO backtracks on rule for displaced residents to leave appliances in temporary housing

item.title: China’s foreign affairs ministry in Hong Kong summons UK, US representatives over remarks on Jimmy Lai conviction
item.description: China’s foreign affairs ministry in Hong Kong has summoned the representatives of the US and the UK consulates general following “interfering” remarks made on the conviction of pro-democracy media mogul Jimmy Lai. item.title: University of Hong Kong denies fire vigil venue, citing instability, ‘force majeure’
item.description: The University of Hong Kong (HKU) denied student bodies the use of a venue to mourn the victims of the deadly Tai Po fire, citing social instability and “force majeure,” a student publication has said. item.title: 100 Guangdong cars expected to enter Hong Kong’s urban areas on Tue under new cross-border travel scheme
item.description: A hundred cars from Guangdong province are expected to enter Hong Kong’s urban areas on Tuesday – the first batch of mainland Chinese vehicles to drive into the city under a new cross-border travel scheme. item.title: EU condemns China’s dairy duties as ‘unjustified’
item.description: The European Union hit out at China on Monday, saying it was “unjustified” for Beijing to impose duties of up to 42.7 percent on some dairy products from the 27-nation bloc. China’s announcement on Monday was the latest in a trade spat with the EU covering a series of goods from food to electric vehicles. […]

item.description: The parents of a man accused of killing three people in a stabbing rampage in a Taiwan metro last week knelt and apologised on Tuesday, promising full cooperation with investigators.
